bbglow.title: The BB Glow Treatment in Aesthetics
bbglow.metaTitle: The BB Glow Treatment in Aesthetics — My Bubble Beauty
bbglow.description: The BB Glow treatment aims to improve the look of the complexion, even out skin tone and give the skin a radiant, fresh appearance. Procedure and prices.
bbglow.articleHtml:
The BB Glow treatment in aesthetics is a skincare technique aimed at improving the complexion, making the skin tone more even, reducing imperfections, and giving the skin a radiant and fresh look. The name refers to BB cream (Blemish Balm), as the treatment likewise aims for a more even-looking complexion.

Skin Preparation

Prior to the treatment, the skin is thoroughly cleansed to remove impurities, sebum, and dead skin cells. The treatment may include a mild exfoliation for better product absorption.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment or damaged skin.

Application of Serums

Specially formulated serums for the BB Glow treatment are applied to the skin. These serums typically contain ingredients such as pigments, hyaluronic acid, peptides, and vitamins. Pigments help even out the skin tone, conceal imperfections, and provide a more radiant complexion.

Microneedling

Microneedling is an essential part of the BB Glow treatment. This technique entails using a device with fine needles to create micro-perforations in the skin. These micro-perforations facilitate better serum absorption and may also stimulate collagen production, contributing to improved skin texture.

Application

After microneedling is completed, a soothing mask or additional treatments may be applied to calm the skin and enhance the benefits of the treatment.

Masks and Targeted Treatments

Cleansing masks or other targeted treatments can be used to soothe the skin, reduce excess sebum, and promote better sebum production regulation.

Hydration and Sun Protection

The treatment is typically concluded with the application of moisturizing products and sun protection to safeguard the newly treated skin from UV rays.

The results of the BB Glow treatment can vary from person to person, but generally, clients report an improvement in skin texture, a reduction in the visibility of imperfections, a more even complexion, and a brighter skin tone. The effects of the treatment are temporary and may last for several weeks to a few months, depending on the skin type and aftercare.

figures.alt: Woman's face with BB Glow foundation swatches on the cheek

charbon.title: Activated Carbon Laser
charbon.metaTitle: Activated Carbon Laser — My Bubble Beauty
charbon.description: Laser treatment with activated carbon aims to improve the appearance of certain skin imperfections, such as pigmented spots. Procedure and prices.
charbon.articleHtml:
Activated carbon is sometimes used in combination with laser treatments to improve the appearance of certain skin imperfections. Laser treatment can help reduce the appearance of various marks on the skin, including pigmentation and tattoos. Here's how a laser treatment with activated carbon typically works:

Application of Activated Carbon

A mask based on activated carbon is applied to the area of the skin to be treated. Activated carbon absorbs laser light, allowing for more targeted treatment of pigmentation or tattoos.

Laser Treatment

Subsequently, the laser is used to emit pulses of intense light in fractions of a second. This light is selectively absorbed by pigment particles, such as tattoo pigments or melanin in pigmented spots.

Pigment Fragmentation

When the laser light is absorbed by the pigments, its energy is converted into heat, leading to the fragmentation of the pigments into smaller particles.

Natural Removal

The fragmented pigment particles are then naturally eliminated by the body over time, primarily through the lymphatic system.

Results

The final outcome depends on the type of skin imperfection concerned. For tattoos, for example, the laser can help break down tattoo pigments, allowing the body to gradually remove them and reduce the appearance of the tattoo. For pigmented spots, this treatment can help lighten or fade the spots.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment or damaged skin.

It's important to note that laser treatments, regardless of the specific technique used, should be performed by a qualified aesthetic professional. These professionals can assess your skin, determine the appropriate treatment method, and ensure that the treatment is performed with risks kept to a minimum, for a result suited to your skin. If you are considering a laser treatment for a specific skin issue, we recommend consulting an aesthetic professional to discuss your specific needs and obtain detailed information about the treatment.

figures.alt: Client wearing a carbon mask and protective goggles during a laser treatment

cire.title: Waxing Unwanted Hair
cire.metaTitle: Waxing Unwanted Hair — My Bubble Beauty
cire.description: Waxing with warm or lukewarm wax pulls hair out by the root, for skin that stays smooth for longer than after shaving. Procedure and prices.
cire.articleHtml:
Waxing unwanted hair is a commonly used method for hair removal in the field of beauty care. This technique involves the application of warm or lukewarm wax to the skin, allowing it to harden and then swiftly removing it, along with the hair. Here's how waxing typically works in beauty care:

Preparation

Before waxing begins, the skin is usually thoroughly cleaned to remove dirt, oil, and cosmetic products. It's important for the skin to be clean and dry before the wax is applied.

Application

The wax is heated to make it liquid but should not be too hot to avoid burns. It is then applied to the area to be waxed using a stick or spatula. The wax adheres to the hair and the skin.

Hardening

The wax is allowed to harden for a few moments. During this period, the wax adheres to the hair, completely covering it.

Removal

Once the wax has hardened, a beauty professional grips an edge of the wax and quickly pulls it off against the direction of hair growth. This action pulls the hair out by the root, leaving the skin temporarily smooth and hair-free.

Aftercare

After waxing, it's common to apply a soothing lotion or moisturizing cream to calm the skin and minimize irritation. Hair gradually regrows, usually within a few weeks.

Waxing can be applied to various parts of the body, including legs, underarms, the bikini line, the face, and other areas with unwanted hair. This hair removal method offers several benefits, such as skin that stays smooth for longer than after shaving, since the hair is pulled out by the root. However, there are also potential downsides, such as the pain associated with hair removal and the possibility of skin irritation.

There are different types of wax, including hot wax, lukewarm wax, and cold wax, each with its own pros and cons. Some people also choose to wax at home using commercially available wax kits, although this may require some practice for good results.

For waxing, it's recommended to seek an experienced professional, especially for sensitive areas, to reduce the risk of injuries or skin irritation.

figures.alt: Golden depilatory wax dripping from a spatula

dents.title: Teeth Whitening
dents.description: Teeth whitening is a cosmetic treatment that aims to lighten the colour of the teeth and reduce stains. Procedure, precautions and prices.
dents.articleHtml:
Teeth whitening is a cosmetic treatment designed to brighten the colour of teeth, making them whiter and brighter. This treatment is commonly performed in aesthetic dentistry to enhance the appearance of a smile by reducing stains and discolourations on the teeth. Here is how teeth whitening works in aesthetics:

Initial Evaluation

Before the teeth whitening process begins, a dentist or aesthetic professional conducts an initial evaluation to determine whether the treatment is suitable for you. Some individuals may not qualify due to underlying dental issues.

Preparation

First, your teeth are cleaned to remove plaque and tartar, which could hinder the bleaching process.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment, sensitive teeth or irritated gums.

Whitening Options

At-Home Whitening: The dentist may provide an at-home whitening kit with custom-made trays and a bleaching gel containing a low concentration of hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide. You fill the trays with the gel and wear them for a specified period daily over a few weeks. This is a gradual process.

In-Office Whitening: This method is also known as professional in-chair bleaching. The dentist applies a more concentrated bleaching gel to your teeth and then uses a special light or a laser to activate the gel. This process is usually faster and may provide immediate results.

Aftercare

After whitening, you may be advised to avoid certain potentially staining foods and beverages (such as coffee, tea, and red wine) for a while to maintain the results. Good oral care, including regular brushing and flossing, is also essential.

Mechanism of Teeth Whitening

The fundamental principle of teeth whitening is based on the use of products containing hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide. These chemicals penetrate the tooth enamel and react with the molecules responsible for stains and discolourations, breaking them down to brighten the teeth's colour. However, it's important to note that teeth whitening is not permanent, and the results can vary from person to person, depending on various factors, including the type of tooth stains and dietary habits.

Pre-Treatment Advice

It is highly recommended to consult a dentist or an aesthetic dental professional before considering teeth whitening, as it may not be suitable for everyone, especially those with existing dental issues. Furthermore, teeth whitening should be performed under the supervision of a professional to help ensure the safety and effectiveness of the treatment.

figures.alt: Smile before and after teeth whitening

hifu.title: High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) in Aesthetics
hifu.metaTitle: HIFU in Aesthetics — My Bubble Beauty
hifu.description: HIFU (High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound) uses focused ultrasound waves to heat the tissues beneath the skin and stimulate collagen production.
hifu.articleHtml:
High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) is a technology that uses high-intensity focused ultrasound waves to heat underlying tissues at specific depths while generally sparing the skin's surface. This heat induces coagulation in the tissues, stimulating collagen production and potentially improving skin firmness.

Applications in Aesthetics

HIFU is used in aesthetics to address various skin concerns and rejuvenation goals, including skin tightening, reducing wrinkles and fine lines, as well as non-surgical facelifts. It can help reduce sagging skin and improve skin firmness on the face, neck, and other body areas. HIFU can decrease the appearance of wrinkles and fine lines by stimulating collagen production. It is sometimes referred to as the "HIFU facelift" due to its tightening effects, achieved without surgery and usually with minimal to no downtime. However, it is not a substitute for a surgical facelift.

How the Treatment Works

During a HIFU session, a device delivers intensely focused ultrasound waves at precise depths within the target tissues. This ultrasound energy heats the underlying tissues and stimulates collagen production. Results are typically not immediately visible but gradually improve over weeks and months as collagen regenerates.

Safety and Comfort

HIFU is considered a non-invasive treatment and generally has few side effects. You may feel a warming sensation during the session, but the treatment is generally well tolerated and usually does not require anaesthesia.

Number of Sessions

The number of sessions required depends on the specific treatment and your goals. In general, several sessions may be recommended for the best results.

Results

HIFU results are gradual and can last for several months. The skin may become firmer, wrinkles may be reduced, and the face can appear tighter.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment or damaged skin.

HIFU is a popular choice in aesthetics for those who want to tighten the skin without surgery. However, as with any aesthetic treatment, it's important to consult a qualified healthcare professional to discuss the right options based on your individual needs and ensure that HIFU is the best solution for you.

hydra.title: HydraFacial
hydra.description: A HydraFacial is a non-invasive aesthetic treatment that aims to improve the appearance of facial skin through cleansing, exfoliation and hydration.
hydra.articleHtml:
A HydraFacial is a non-invasive aesthetic treatment designed to improve the appearance of facial skin by combining various techniques, including exfoliation, deep cleansing, hydration, and protection. It is designed to soften the look of various skin concerns such as blemishes on acne-prone skin, wrinkles, pigmentation spots, and uneven skin texture.

Working Principle

Cleansing: The process begins with a deep cleansing of the skin to remove impurities, excess sebum, and dead skin cells.

Exfoliation: Next, a gentle exfoliating solution is applied to the skin to remove dead skin cells from the skin's surface for a fresher, smoother complexion.

Extraction: The HydraFacial system uses gentle suction to remove impurities from the skin pores, which can help reduce blemishes and unclog pores.

Hydration: Subsequently, a hydrating solution enriched with antioxidants, peptides, and hyaluronic acid is applied to deeply nourish and moisturize the skin.

Protection: Finally, sunscreen or sun protection products are often applied to protect the freshly treated skin from harmful UV rays.

Results

The entire treatment is relatively quick and minimally uncomfortable. Many describe it as enjoyable and relaxing. Results from a HydraFacial can vary from person to person. The treatment aims for an immediate improvement in the appearance of the skin, with a brighter, softer complexion and a more even tone.

Source: HydraFacial UK

figures.alt: Beautician performing a HydraFacial treatment on a client's face

laserepilation.title: Long-Lasting Laser Hair Removal in Aesthetics
laserepilation.metaTitle: Long-Lasting Laser Hair Removal in Aesthetics — My Bubble Beauty
laserepilation.description: Long-lasting laser hair removal uses light absorbed by the melanin in the hair to slow regrowth. Several sessions, a few weeks apart, are needed.
laserepilation.articleHtml:
Laser hair removal works by using a specific laser that emits intense light radiation. This light is absorbed by the melanin in the hair follicles. The energy absorbed by the melanin is converted into heat, which damages the hair follicles, inhibiting future hair growth.

Types of Lasers

Various types of lasers are used for laser hair removal, including Alexandrite lasers, Nd:YAG lasers, and diode lasers. The choice often depends on your skin and hair colour.

Laser Hair Removal Session

During a laser hair removal session, the aesthetic professional applies the laser to the area being treated. You will typically wear protective goggles to shield your eyes from the intense light. The session can be somewhat uncomfortable but is generally well tolerated by most clients.

Series of Sessions

Laser hair removal is not a one-time treatment. To achieve optimal results, multiple sessions are required at intervals of several weeks, as hair grows in different cycles.

Results

The results of laser hair removal vary from person to person, but many clients notice a significant reduction in hair growth after several sessions. A substantial portion of the hair can be removed for the long term, although occasional touch-ups may be needed to treat any remaining hair.

Safety

Laser hair removal is generally considered a safe treatment when performed by a qualified professional. Common side effects are temporary and may include redness, warmth, or itching in the treated area.

Benefits

Laser hair removal offers many benefits, including long-lasting hair reduction, smooth skin, and a reduced need for shaving or waxing.

Prior Consultation

Before undergoing laser hair removal, it is recommended to consult an aesthetic professional to assess your skin type, hair colour, and suitability for the treatment.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment or damaged skin.

Laser hair removal is a popular choice for those looking to reduce unwanted hair over the long term. However, it is essential to consult a qualified professional to discuss expectations, potential results, and precautions before undergoing this treatment.

lipolaser.title: Lipo Laser
lipolaser.description: Laser lipolysis, or "lipo laser", is a non-invasive aesthetic treatment that aims to reduce body fat in target areas such as the abdomen, thighs and arms.
lipolaser.articleHtml:
Laser lipolysis, also known as "lipo laser", is a non-invasive aesthetic treatment aimed at reducing body fat, primarily in target areas such as the abdomen, thighs, arms, or flanks. Here is how a lipo laser treatment usually works:

Initial Consultation

Prior to a lipo laser treatment, you'll have an initial consultation with an aesthetic professional. During this consultation, your fat loss goals and the areas to be treated are discussed, and basic health and fitness information is taken into consideration.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment or damaged skin.

Preparation

On the day of the treatment, the treatment area is cleansed. Photos may be taken to track progress over time.

Application of Lasers

Lipo laser devices contain diodes that emit low-intensity laser light. They are placed directly on the skin of the treatment area. These lasers emit specific wavelengths that are absorbed by the fat cells beneath the skin.

Action on Fat Cells

The lasers are intended to stimulate the fat cells to encourage the release of their contents. This process is known as lipolysis, where fat cells release their triglycerides as fatty acids and glycerol.

Removal of Fats

The fatty acids and glycerol released during lipolysis are naturally eliminated by the body. This can occur through the lymphatic system and the liver.

Post-Treatment

After the lipo laser session, it is often recommended to engage in physical activity to help burn the released fats. It is also important to stay well hydrated to facilitate fat removal.

Multiple Sessions

One lipo laser treatment may yield slight results, so multiple sessions are usually needed to see more noticeable results, which vary from person to person. These sessions are typically scheduled several weeks apart.

It's important to note that lipo laser is intended for reducing body fat, but it is not a substitute for a balanced diet and exercise. To maintain the results, a healthy lifestyle is essential.

figures.alt: Diagram comparing skin with cellulite before and after a course of lipo laser

mado.title: Maderotherapy
mado.description: Maderotherapy is a massage using wooden tools that aims to smooth the skin and reduce the appearance of cellulite. Find out how it works and the price.
mado.articleHtml:
Maderotherapy is a body massage and shaping technique that uses specially designed wooden tools, such as rollers, sticks, and wooden spoons, to improve skin texture, reduce the appearance of cellulite, and promote relaxation. The term "maderotherapy" is derived from the Spanish word "madera", which means wood, and "therapy".

Preparation

Before the treatment, the practitioner discusses your goals and concerns with you. Then, massage oil or lotion is applied to the skin to facilitate the gliding of the wooden tools.

Massage with Wooden Tools

The practitioner uses specially designed wooden tools to perform various types of massage techniques. These wooden tools come in various shapes and sizes suitable for different body parts and massage methods. Movements can be kneading, rolling, pressing, or circular, depending on the treatment goals.

Effects

Maderotherapy aims to work on areas of localized fullness, smooth the skin, improve skin texture, and promote muscle relaxation. It can also be used to address areas of the body with cellulite.

Multiple Sessions

To achieve optimal results, multiple maderotherapy sessions are typically required. The frequency of sessions depends on your goals and the condition of your skin.

Maderotherapy is often considered a non-invasive and relaxing treatment, although the sensations during the treatment may vary depending on the applied pressure and treated areas. The benefits of maderotherapy may include firmer, more toned skin and a reduction in the appearance of cellulite.

As with any aesthetic treatment, it is recommended to consult a qualified professional to discuss your specific needs, benefits, and potential risks of maderotherapy, as well as to assess whether this treatment is suitable for your situation.

figures.alt: Leg massage with a wooden maderotherapy roller

microneed.title: Microneedling/Micropen
microneed.description: Microneedling uses fine needles to make tiny, controlled openings in the skin to improve its texture and appearance. Find out how it works and the price.
microneed.articleHtml:
Microneedling/Micropen is an aesthetic treatment that utilizes a device with fine needles to create controlled, tiny openings in the skin. This technique is also known as microperforation. Here's how microneedling works:

Preparation

Prior to the treatment, your aesthetic professional thoroughly cleanses your skin, and a numbing gel may be applied to minimize discomfort. The needle depth is adjusted based on your specific needs and the areas to be treated.

Micro-Punctures

The microneedling device is gently moved across the skin, creating small punctures. These punctures are so tiny that they are usually barely visible to the naked eye. The device typically features various needle lengths to reach different layers of the skin, depending on the goal of the treatment.

Stimulation of Collagen

The microperforations aim to stimulate the skin's natural response, in particular the production of collagen and elastin. Collagen is an essential protein that provides firmness and elasticity to the skin, while elastin helps keep the skin supple. This collagen stimulation may help improve the skin's texture and appearance.

Aftercare

Following the treatment, your aesthetic professional may apply specific topical products, such as moisturizing serums or growth factors, to soothe and hydrate the skin. It is also recommended to avoid excessive sun exposure and use sunscreen to protect the freshly treated skin.

Benefits

Microneedling can be used to improve the appearance of a variety of skin issues, including wrinkles and fine lines, acne scars, pigment spots, loss of skin firmness, and other skin imperfections. Results are usually not immediately visible, as collagen production takes time. You may notice gradual improvements in the appearance of your skin in the weeks following the treatment.

Multiple Sessions

The number of sessions required depends on your treatment goals and the condition of your skin. Your aesthetic professional will create a customized treatment plan to meet your specific needs.

Prior Consultation

It is important to consult a qualified professional for microneedling, as improper device usage or unsuitable needles can lead to complications. This treatment is typically considered safe when performed by an experienced professional.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment or damaged skin.

figures.alt: Diagram of the skin before microneedling
Diagram of the skin during microneedling: the pen creates tiny perforations
Diagram of the skin during microneedling: a serum penetrates through the perforations
Diagram of the skin four to six weeks after microneedling

peeling.title: Superficial Peel
peeling.description: A superficial peel is a gentle exfoliating treatment that aims to improve skin texture and even out skin tone. Find out how it works and the price.
peeling.articleHtml:
A superficial peel is an aesthetic treatment aimed at improving skin texture, creating a more even tone, and reducing certain minor skin issues such as pigmentation, fine lines, and blemishes on acne-prone skin. This technique uses a mild chemical solution to exfoliate the top layer of the skin, with the aim of stimulating cell renewal and promoting smoother, more radiant skin. Here's how a superficial peel usually works:

Initial Consultation

Prior to a superficial peel, an aesthetic professional assesses the condition of your skin, discusses your specific concerns, and determines whether the peel is suitable for your skin type and needs. There are various types of chemical solutions for peels, and the choice depends on your skin type and the treatment's purpose.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment or damaged skin.

Skin Cleansing

Before applying the peel solution, the skin is carefully cleansed to remove dirt, makeup, and oils.

Application of the Peel Solution

Next, the aesthetic professional applies the peel solution to the skin, ensuring that the treated area is evenly covered. The solution may contain alpha hydroxy acids (AHAs), beta hydroxy acids (BHAs), or other mild exfoliating ingredients.

Contact Time

The peel solution remains on the skin for a short time determined by the professional, usually for several minutes. The duration depends on the solution's concentration and your skin's tolerance.

Neutralization

After the contact time has passed, the professional neutralizes the solution by rinsing it off or using a specific product to stop the chemical action.

Post-Peel Care

After the treatment, it's essential to follow the post-peel instructions provided by the aesthetic professional. This may include applying a moisturizing cream, using specific products, and avoiding sun exposure for some time, as the skin is often more sensitive after a peel.

Results

The results of a superficial peel are usually not immediately visible, as the skin needs time to renew itself. However, in the days and weeks following the treatment, the skin should appear brighter, more even, and smoother.

A superficial peel is considered a mild treatment and typically doesn't require extended recovery time. However, multiple sessions may be necessary to achieve the desired results, and it's essential to choose a qualified professional to minimize risks and optimize the benefits of the treatment. This treatment can be applied to various body parts, such as the face, neck, décolletage, and hands, depending on your needs.

Diagram of the skin during the peel: the solution is applied with a cotton bud
Diagram of the skin a few days after the peel

photo.title: Phototherapy
photo.description: Phototherapy, also known as light therapy, is used in aesthetics to improve the appearance of the skin. Discover how a session works and what it costs.
photo.articleHtml:
Phototherapy, also known as light therapy, is a technique used in aesthetics to improve the appearance of the skin and reduce the visibility of various imperfections by utilizing different wavelengths of light. Phototherapy can be performed using various devices, including LED lamps or lasers. This is how phototherapy typically works in aesthetics:

Wavelength Selection

Phototherapy involves using light at a specific wavelength depending on the treatment goal. Different wavelengths target different skin issues. For example, red light is often used to stimulate collagen production and improve skin texture, while blue light is used to help purify acne-prone skin.

Skin Preparation

Prior to phototherapy, the skin must be clean and free from cosmetics. Clients often wear protective eyewear to shield their eyes from intense light.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment or damaged skin.

Phototherapy Session

The aesthetic professional uses the phototherapy device to expose the skin to light at the specific wavelength for a certain duration. The light is usually evenly applied to the area being treated.

Skin Response

The light penetrates the skin and interacts with the target cells, which can have various beneficial effects, such as stimulating collagen production, soothing the skin, purifying acne-prone skin, or reducing the appearance of excessive pigmentation.

Aftercare

After the phototherapy session, it may be necessary to apply soothing or moisturizing topical products to calm the skin and minimize irritation. Sun protection is also essential after treatment, as the skin may be more sensitive to sun damage.

Results

Phototherapy is used to improve the appearance of a wide range of skin issues, including acne-prone skin, wrinkles, pigment spots, and scars. The benefits of phototherapy generally include little to no downtime and gradual results.

Duration

The duration of the treatment and the number of sessions required vary depending on the treatment goal and the individual skin response. It is important to consult with a qualified aesthetic professional to discuss your specific needs and determine if phototherapy is suitable for you.

figures.alt: Client's face under a red LED panel

plasma.title: The Plasma Pen / Micropen
plasma.metaTitle: The Plasma Pen / Micropen — My Bubble Beauty
plasma.description: The plasma pen / micropen is an aesthetic device that aims to improve the appearance of sagging skin, wrinkles, scars and pigmentation spots.
plasma.articleHtml:
The plasma pen / micropen is a relatively recent aesthetic treatment device used to improve the appearance of various skin concerns, including sagging skin, wrinkles, scars, stretch marks, and pigmentation spots. This device works by generating a plasma arc on the skin's surface, resulting in controlled micro-injuries. This is how the plasma pen typically works in aesthetics:

Basic Principle

The plasma pen uses electrical energy to create a thin, hot plasma arc at the tip of the pen. Plasma is ionized gas composed of charged particles, which means it contains ions and free electrons.

Application

The aesthetic professional uses the plasma pen to treat specific areas of the skin. When the pen's tip touches the skin, the plasma arc is directed onto the skin's surface, creating extremely small, burning micro-points on the skin while limiting the impact on the surrounding tissues.

Skin Tightening

The application of plasma can result in immediate skin tightening as the generated heat causes contraction of collagen fibres in the treated area. This can help reduce the appearance of sagging skin.

Formation of Scabs and Micro-Injuries

The micro-points created by the plasma pen also lead to the formation of scabs on the skin. In the days following the treatment, these scabs naturally fall off, revealing new skin underneath. During this recovery phase, the skin also produces additional collagen, which can improve skin texture and overall appearance.

Results

The results of the plasma pen can vary depending on the targeted skin concern and the depth at which the device is used. You may see improvements in the appearance of your skin over time as the effects of collagen become visible. However, multiple sessions may be needed to achieve optimal results.

It's important to note that the plasma pen is an invasive treatment, albeit less invasive than some other aesthetic treatments. You may experience some discomfort during the treatment, but local anaesthetics are typically applied to minimize this discomfort.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment or damaged skin.

The plasma pen should be used by trained and experienced aesthetic professionals, as improper use can lead to complications or scarring. As with any aesthetic treatment, it's recommended to consult with an aesthetic professional to discuss your specific needs and determine if the plasma pen is suitable for you.

radiofrequence.title: Radiofrequency
radiofrequence.description: Radiofrequency is an aesthetic technology that uses electromagnetic waves to gently heat the deep layers of the skin.
radiofrequence.articleHtml:
Radiofrequency is an aesthetic technology that uses electromagnetic waves to gently heat the deep layers of the skin. This heat aims to stimulate collagen production, boost blood circulation and promote skin tightening.

Applications in Aesthetics

Radiofrequency is used in aesthetics to address various skin concerns and rejuvenation goals, including skin tightening, reducing wrinkles and fine lines, softening the appearance of cellulite, and improving skin texture. It can help reduce skin sagging and enhance firmness. Increased collagen production helps smooth out wrinkles and fine lines. It can aid in reducing the visibility of cellulite by stimulating circulation and promoting lymphatic drainage. Radiofrequency can also improve overall skin texture by reducing the appearance of acne scars and imperfections.

How the Treatment Works

During a radiofrequency treatment, a device emits electromagnetic waves into the targeted skin. This energy is converted into heat, warming the underlying tissues while sparing the skin's surface as much as possible. The heat aims to stimulate collagen production and the skin's natural renewal. The results are usually not immediately visible but gradually improve over time as collagen regenerates.

Safety and Comfort

Radiofrequency is a non-invasive treatment, meaning it doesn't require surgery or incisions. You will typically feel a warm sensation during the session, but the treatment is generally well tolerated and does not require anaesthesia.

Number of Sessions

The number of sessions needed depends on the specific treatment and your goals. In general, multiple sessions may be recommended for the best results.

Results

The results of radiofrequency in aesthetics are progressive and can last for several months. The skin may appear firmer, wrinkles may look softened, and overall skin texture may improve.

Before the treatment, we check with you for any contraindications, such as pregnancy, ongoing medical treatment or damaged skin.

Radiofrequency is a popular option in aesthetics due to the results it can offer and its non-invasive nature. It is used to address various skin issues and may be an attractive non-surgical option for some individuals looking to enhance their appearance. However, it is always recommended to consult with a qualified aesthetic professional before undergoing an aesthetic treatment to discuss suitable options based on individual needs.

sos.title: SOS Purity Treatment
sos.metaTitle: SOS Purity Treatment — My Bubble Beauty
sos.description: The SOS Purity treatment aims to deeply cleanse oily, acne-prone skin, reduce excess sebum and unclog pores. Discover how a session works.
sos.articleHtml:
An SOS Purity treatment in aesthetics is specially designed for individuals with skin issues related to excess sebum, a tendency towards acne, blackheads, and other skin imperfections. This type of treatment aims to deeply cleanse the skin, reduce excess sebum, unclog pores, and promote clearer and healthier skin. Here's how an SOS Purity treatment in aesthetics may work:

Deep Cleansing

The treatment typically begins with a thorough cleansing of the face to remove impurities, excess sebum, and dead skin cells.

Exfoliation

Gentle exfoliation may be performed to eliminate dead skin cells, promoting smoother skin.

Blackhead Extraction

Aestheticians or skin professionals often use manual extraction techniques or extraction devices to remove blackheads and comedones. This helps unclog pores and improve skin texture.

Application of Suitable Products

Specific products containing ingredients such as salicylic acid, known for its purifying properties, may be applied to the skin to help calm redness and limit the appearance of new blemishes.

Masks and Targeted Treatments

Purifying masks or other targeted treatments may be used to soothe the skin, reduce excess sebum, and promote better sebum production regulation.

Hydration

Even if you have skin issues related to excess sebum, it's essential to maintain proper skin hydration to prevent it from becoming too dry in response to treatments. Lightweight and non-comedogenic moisturizing products can be used.

Sun Protection

As with many skin treatments, applying sunscreen or sun protection products is important to shield the skin from UV damage.
